newsitem.title: USA: Attorneys say settlement will not affect Fla. case.
newsitem.headline: Attorneys say settlement will not affect Fla. case.

text.p: Attorneys representing three tobacco companies said on Friday their clients told them the so-called "global" tobacco talks would not affect a class action case in which flight attendants are suing tobacco companies over illnesses allegedly linked to second-hand smoke.

"I have been told that I am free to tell the court that this case is going forward," David Hardy, an attorney for Philip Morris Cos Inc. and Lorillard said before jury selection resumed in the case known as Norma Broin vs. Philip Morris Cos Inc. et al. Edward Moss, an attorney for Brown & Williamson, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, said the firm he represents would say the same.
Hardy said he had asked Philip Morris if the settlement talks would affect the Broin case. "The response from Philip Morris was 'No,'" he said. "The case can go forward."
Hardy, who also represents Lorillard Tobacco Co., added: "I know Lorillard's position is the same because I represent them, too."
Lorillard is a unit of Loews Corp..
Edward Moss, who is representing Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp., said: "That's the same for Brown & Williamson."
